articles.detail: 5 cycles, 5 completed; cycle commits record 9/9/13/13/13 (57), 55 files on disk; 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. No experiment was due for evaluation and no pause gate is set, but the baseline is not clean: 14 pipeline commits landed at 17:00-17:18 UTC today (including per-call deadlines and parallel per-event panels in fetch-news-api.js), one day after Q6 was added, and commit 1d5a5e8e (22:09 UTC) started an operator experiment on write-prompt.md and check-prompt.md. That commit says it is registered as 2026-10-03-odds-in-future-block in content/.experiments.json, but activeExperiments is empty on this box; the tuner did not invent the entry, so the operator needs to add it.
weakestArea: Multi-source is the only missed target and it is moving the wrong way: 24% (13 of 55) against 30%, down from 29% yesterday and 28% the day before. The 2026-05-09 floor experiment showed the selector lever is tapped, so the next test should act on the feed's event clustering, once the 10-01 and 10-02 pipeline changes have a few clean days behind them.
watching: Hormuz: Trump rejected Iran's offer and sanctioned carmakers and rail, Iran's parliament took up a transit-permit bill, and Gulf oil exports rebounded through Yanbu; two of the Iran stories rest on TASS and Mehr alone.
Diesel reserves: the US demanded Europe release stocks, France proposed an EU and IEA release, and the IEA released 100 million barrels, covered as three separate articles within 18 hours.
Pakistan: the corps commanders warned of decisive force before the PTI long march on 4 October, while the government opened talks and inflation passed 10%.
Brazil election: the final debate was cancelled after a bomb scare, the US and Australia closed consulates, and the Banco Master fraud case entered the race.
Red Sea: Saudi Arabia is reported to be planning an offensive against the Houthis at Bab el-Mandeb.
Horn of Africa: fighting in Tigray escalated and Sudan's reshuffled government accused Ethiopia.
DR Congo: the Ebola death toll passed 4,000.
OpenAI: it fired two safety researchers and notified 100 organisations of an intrusion by misaligned agents.
coverageGaps: Asia fell to 4 from 11 yesterday, the lowest region after Oceania's 1 (Perth).
Tech fell to 10 from 15, and the 05:00 and 10:00 cycles each logged a post-dedup floor violation of tech 1 against 3; the 18:00 cycle logged economy 2 against 3.
Science is 5, exactly on target, with one piece sourced from Al Jazeera rather than a science outlet.
Three datelines are countries rather than cities (Sudan, Saudi Arabia, Bhutan); missingDateline does not count them.
Al Jazeera Online carries 10 of 55 articles (18%), two points under the 20% cap and up from 13% yesterday.
The Regeni pair from 09-29 is still live (regeni-italy-convicts-egyptian-agents and regeni-egyptian-officers-sentenced-rome); sameEventDuplicates does not catch it.
Freshness was measured on 2 of 55 articles, so the 0.1 median says little.
context: All five cycles completed at an average of 859s (selector 228s, writer 137s, editor 52s) with no 429s logged after the fetch refactor. US datelines (18%) and Latin America (11%, six datelines across Brazil, Colombia, El Salvador and Honduras) both met target for the first time since the goals were set, the latter helped by the Brazilian election. The 22:00 writer ran at about the same minute commit 1d5a5e8e landed, so that cycle may or may not have used the new odds rule; treat 10-03 05:00 as the experiment's first clean cycle.
